ocr_text: ATP Hangzhou R1 The underdog that holds the most appeal in Hangzhou's R1 matches is local player Yibing Wu, who takes on veteran French lefty Adrian Mannarino. Wu is from Hanzghou and will clearly be hugely motivated to play here and he's been showing some good form since coming back from yet another injury issue. Wu beat Moutet, Popyrin and Monfils in similar conditions in Washington DC and after that failed to qualify for the US Open, but lost only in the final round to the in-form Jerome Kym, who went on to have an impressive tournament. Wu's career has been blighted by injuries, but when he's fit he's so dangerous, and he beat Mannarino easily in their only career meeting in quick conditions in Dallas. Wu won that match by 116 to 84 in terms of service points won/return points won totals and Mannarino won just 26% of return points and 33% of second serve points. Manna has had a late resurgence to a career that looked to be all but over a few months ago, but what has the big effort this hard court summer taken out of his 37-year-old body? irie played 13 matches in 6 weeks and I wonder if he'll be as motivated as Wu for this part of the tour. It's all about fitness with Wu and you'd think he'd have prioritised this week, so I'm happy to beat him as underdog here. RECOMMENDATION 1 point win - Wu to beat Mannarino or Bet Victor Cappellabed (+120) with Betfred, Bet 365
